era.title: Essential decisions do not need a cloud round trip.
era.subtitle: Sensing, decisions and control that can happen on site stay on site. Response is faster, essentials work offline, and the data boundary is easier to understand.
era.col1Body: Inference returns to a place you can see, a plug you can pull.
era.col2Body: Before you speak, it is already watching, listening, preparing.
era.col3Body: An intelligence grown for you, your family, your space -- no one else.

nightCare.title: Nighttime bed-exit response loop
nightCare.subtitle: A complete event record from bed-exit detection and risk escalation through care response and information sharing.

spectrum.title: Get the bedside, desk and living room right first.
spectrum.subtitle: The same local rules can grow from one room to a home or community, but each step begins with specific devices and a specific need.
spectrum.bedsideBody: The first light, that understands your night.
spectrum.deskBody: The room prepared, before the thought arrives.
spectrum.homeBody: A house that understands the people living in it.
spectrum.communityBody: A building, a street -- looking out for each other, without looking in.

intelligence.title: Know who is present. Then run the right rule.
intelligence.subtitle: The system distinguishes household members, rooms and time before following an approved rule. One vague command does not decide for everyone.
intelligence.card1Body: Read room conditions and device changes.
intelligence.card2Body: Store personal preferences with explicit permission.
intelligence.card3Body: Connect each trigger to its resulting action.
intelligence.card4Body: Route an approved rule to the right device.
intelligence.cta: Meet the intelligence that is yours

vision.title: Keep sensing, decisions and control in the room.
vision.body: The system reads device state, runs local rules and keeps records on site. When a cloud service is required, it says so clearly instead of treating connectivity as a given.

platform.title: AIOS local intelligence system platform
platform.subtitle: From sensing to action, every step has a clear input, rule and result.
platform.sensingBody: Processes voice, environmental sensors, device state and spatial events through one event layer.
platform.edgeBody: State evaluation and core controls run on-site without depending on the public internet.
platform.memoryBody: Static facts, live state, recurring patterns and semantic information are managed separately.
platform.protocolsBody: Connects approved mainstream devices and protocols through adapters.
platform.privacyBody: Data stays home by default; when the network drops, the essentials keep running.

trust.title: Every rule and every action leaves a record.
trust.body: The local audit record shows when a rule changed, who approved it and whether the device completed the action. Families, managers and regulators only see what their role permits.

hero.title: A local intelligence kernel for residences
hero.subtitle: Handles device integration, state management, rule suggestions and control on site. Locks, alerts and other high-risk actions retain human approval.

section.title: Four capability groups
section.body: Functions are organized around household members, site state, device control and data boundaries. Every automation rule remains inspectable and editable.

memory.title: Authorized preference records
memory.body: Common lighting, temperature and routine preferences are stored locally with permission, and can be reviewed, changed or deleted.

personalization.title: Member data isolation
personalization.body: Preferences stay separate by household member. Shared spaces follow household rules instead of applying one person's habits to everyone.

learning.title: Recurring pattern detection
learning.body: When the same action happens repeatedly, the system turns it into a suggestion. It becomes an automation only after approval.

orchestra.title: Common device integration
orchestra.body: Lights, air conditioning, curtains and sensors keep doing their own jobs. AIOS routes approved rules to the right device.

anticipatory.title: Rule approval mechanism
anticipatory.body: Time, presence and recent changes can prompt a suggestion. Locks, alerts and other consequential actions ask for confirmation first.

privacy.title: Process raw data locally first
privacy.body: Sensing data is processed locally by default. You can inspect what was recorded, which rule ran and whether data was allowed to leave.

offline.title: Offline core control
offline.body: Local lighting, device control and configured alert rules continue during an outage. Cloud-dependent services clearly show when unavailable.

household.title: Shared and personal permissions
household.body: The household manages common-area rules together. Bedrooms, routines and personal preferences remain individually controlled, and guests are not added to long-term memory.

hero.title: A complete on-site system, from sensing to action.
hero.subtitle: Gateway, sensing, interaction, connection and action each have a defined role in site state management and device control.

closing.title: Five roles. One complete workflow.
closing.body: The system keeps state input, rule evaluation, device integration, action and result records within one on-site workflow. Clear responsibilities make deployment, acceptance and maintenance easier.
closing.bullet1: Essential state and control paths run on site.
closing.bullet2: Collection scope, device access and action boundaries are configurable.
closing.bullet3: Rule changes, action results and exceptions remain recorded.

hero.title: Plugins and connectors
hero.subtitle: Connect devices, on-site systems and operational workflows. Each plugin states its runtime, permissions, supported products and boundaries.

cta.title: Development and test requirements
cta.body: Review manifest fields, permission scopes, action interfaces, version rules and release checks.

products.title: Products
products.subtitle: Three deployment profiles for homes, community facilities and private hospital environments.

homeBox.name: Home Box
homeBox.desc: A local hub for device integration, rule execution and state management in an individual home.
homeBox.bullet1: Connects approved lighting, locks and environmental devices
homeBox.bullet2: Configures automation by room, member, time and state
homeBox.bullet3: Core controls run locally and remain available offline

communityKit.name: Community Kit
communityKit.desc: A tiered gateway system for senior apartments and community care facilities managing 20-200 units.
communityKit.bullet1: Tiered deployment across community gateways and in-unit nodes
communityKit.bullet2: Role-based access for families, care staff and administrators
communityKit.bullet3: Searchable and exportable event, rule and operation records

enterpriseStack.name: Enterprise Stack
enterpriseStack.desc: An on-premises system for hospitals and large care facilities, integrated with existing systems per project.
enterpriseStack.bullet1: Unified configuration for on-site nodes, permissions and network policy
enterpriseStack.bullet2: Queryable and exportable records for compliance workflows
enterpriseStack.bullet3: Project-defined interfaces to existing information systems

trust.title: Trust & Compliance
trust.subtitle: Inspectable controls from network boundaries and access permissions to operating records and project acceptance.

localFirst.title: Network Boundaries
localFirst.body: Application access, outbound connections, service isolation and host protection are configured for each project. Essential on-site workflows do not require public internet access.

auditChain.title: AuditLedger · Operation Records
auditChain.body: Key decisions, device actions and rule changes are recorded on site for authorized review and project verification.

rbac.title: RBAC · Roles and Multi-site Isolation
rbac.body: Standard role model (admin / operator / observer / user) with multi-site and floor-level access scopes — each person sees only what their role covers.

compliance.title: Project-level Compliance Mapping
compliance.body: Applicable regulation, industry requirements and customer policy determine control points, responsibilities and acceptance evidence for each project.

manifesto.title: Bringing inference back to you.
manifesto.p1: For the last decade we handed more and more to the cloud. It amplified what we could do, and quietly took some things with it -- our latency, our privacy, our sense of how these systems actually work.
manifesto.p2: We think the part of intelligence closest to you should stay close -- on a device you can see, in a place you can unplug. It won't always be the fastest option, but it should be the one you trust.
manifesto.p3: What SidebyStar is building is more than a product. It is a foundation we hope others can build on, so that ambient intelligence can grow naturally in every home, clinic and community.
manifesto.predictions: Three things we think will happen
manifesto.pred1: Every home will have a local intelligence hub, the way every home today has a router.
manifesto.pred2: Being traceable and auditable will become a baseline expectation of AI -- the way HTTPS is today.
manifesto.pred3: More collaboration between devices will happen locally, instead of routing through the cloud.

frontiers.title: What we're researching
frontiers.subtitle: What we've shipped, what is in the lab, and what we hope becomes a standard by 2030.

jepa.title: Visual models that can anticipate
jepa.body: Not only seeing what is happening, but sensing what might happen -- so that an alert can arrive before an incident.

causal.title: Memory that understands causes
causal.body: Going beyond event logs. We record why something happened, and how to avoid it next time.

endSideLlm.title: Small, intimate, on-device models
endSideLlm.body: Lightweight models running directly on local hardware in homes and facilities -- a kernel of intelligence that belongs to that space.

zkAudit.title: Provable compliance, no raw data shared
zkAudit.body: Let facilities prove to regulators that they are compliant, without ever handing over a single line of personal data.

fedBundle.title: Offline profile bundles
fedBundle.body: Industry and site profiles ship as offline tarballs with manifests and checksums; imports preview first, then admins apply to the fact base and audit trail. Identities and sensitive detail stay at the source.

Start with one space.
Validate the complete workflow.
cases.heroBody: A pilot covers device integration, rule configuration, event response and acceptance within one room or floor, providing a clear basis for expansion.
cases.fitSubtitle: Clear scope and ownership produce results that can be reviewed.
cases.fit1: Senior apartments, community-care centers, rehabilitation support wards or residential demonstration spaces
cases.fit2: A single room or floor that can complete validation within two to four weeks
cases.fit3: Named business, site and acceptance owners
cases.fit4: The required network access, device inventory and installation conditions
cases.provide1: Site assessment, solution boundaries and device inventory
cases.provide2: Device configuration, on-site installation, rule integration and operating support
cases.provide3: Acceptance criteria and exception handling agreed with the project team
cases.provide4: Operating records, issue list and expansion recommendations after the pilot
cases.notProvide1: Does not replace care staff or existing ticketing, scheduling and emergency procedures

cases.notProvide3: Customer names, site material and operating data are not published without approval
cases.promise: Each pilot follows a mutually confirmed scope and acceptance criteria. Configuration, operating events, response results and conclusions are recorded to support the next deployment decision.
